propositions.text: Claimant is a Turkish citizen seeking refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX, a citizen of Turkey, claims refugee protection pursuant to sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act1 (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant, a Turkish citizen, seeks refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).

propositions.text: Claimant is a 22-year-old Kurdish man fearing persecution due to political activities, nationality, and military conscription.
propositions.quote: The claimant is a 22-year-old Kurdish (Kurmanji) young man who alleges a fear of persecution if returned to Turkey due to his political activities, his nationality and required military conscription.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is a 22-year-old Kurdish man fearing persecution in Turkey due to political activities, nationality, and conscription.

propositions.text: Claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimant is not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: Claimant's Turkish nationality established by testimony and identity documents including passport and identity cards.
propositions.quote: The claimant's identity as a national of Turkey has been established by his testimony and by the personal identity documents filed, including a certified copy of his Turkish passport issued in XXXX 2010;3 his Turkish National Identity Card,4 a High School Student Identity Card5 and High School diploma.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's Turkish nationality established by testimony and identity documents.

propositions.text: Claimant's sworn facts presumed true unless valid reason to doubt; credibility decided on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: When a claimant swears that certain facts are true, this creates a presumption that they are indeed true unless there is valid reason to doubt their veracity.7 The determination as to whether a claimant's evidence is credible is made on a balance of probabilities.8

propositions.text: Claimant's political profile, detention in 2011, mistreatment, and police interest not credibly established.
propositions.quote: The following aspects of the claimant's story did not establish credible evidence that, * He has the political profile he alleges; * He was detained by Turkish authorities in XXXX 2011 and/or sustained the mistreatment during this detention, or that; * Turkish authorities have any interest in him due to his political activities.

paragraphs.summary: The court states sworn facts are presumed true absent doubt; finds claimant's political profile, detention, mistreatment, and police interest not credible.

propositions.text: Claimant may have been detained at Newroz celebrations in 2006 and 2009 but no credible evidence he was in Turkey in 2011.
propositions.quote: Rather, while I accept that the claimant may have participated in Newroz celebrations which may have resulted in his being detained by police while attending a Newroz celebration in XXXX 20069 and "at random" on XXXX XXXX, 200910 when police were attempting to disperse a protest in front of a court house, I have not been provided with credible or reliable evidence to establish that the claimant was even in Turkey in XXXX 2011.

propositions.text: Claimant embellished the 2011 incident to bolster protection claim.
propositions.quote: This consequently results in finding that the claimant has embellished the precipitating incident of XXXX XXXX, 201111 in efforts to bolster his claim for protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court accepts claimant's detention at Newroz celebrations in 2006 and 2009 but finds no credible evidence he was in Turkey in 2011 and that he embellished that incident.

propositions.text: Claimant failed to provide credible evidence he was in Turkey on alleged dates, which is his responsibility.
propositions.quote: Having reviewed the evidence in its entirety, I find the claimant has not provided any credible evidence to support a finding that he was in Turkey as at the dates he has alleged, which is his responsibility to do.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant failed to provide credible evidence he was in Turkey on alleged dates, his responsibility.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges arrest and beating at March 2011 Newroz celebration by police attacking crowd at random.
propositions.quote: The precipitating incident which the claimant has alleged was his reason for departing Turkey, as presented in his Personal Information Form and narrative is his having been arrested by police who attending a March 2011 Newroz celebration, attacking the crowd and arresting people at random.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges he fell, twisted foot, and was beaten with truncheons while on ground.
propositions.quote: He states that he tried to run away but that he fell and twisted his foot and "that while he was on the ground that the police beat him with truncheons."

propositions.text: Claimant testifies police used tear gas, arrested randomly, detained him two days, beat and tortured him until father picked him up.
propositions.quote: The claimant's testimony indicated that he noticed the police arrive while he was dancing and described the police using tear gas, randomly catching people and beating whomever they caught. He indicated that he was rounded up with many other people and taken to a police station where he was put into a cell for two days, claiming that he was beaten and tortured until his father came to pick him up.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges police arrested and beat him at March 2011 Newroz celebration, detaining him two days and torturing him until his father picked him up.

propositions.text: Claimant was not individually targeted or tortured; police arrested people at random, not protesting as previously stated.
propositions.quote: Having reviewed the evidence regarding this particular incident, I do not find that the claimant was individually targeted by the police for his perceived political opinion, or that he was tortured as he claims. Rather, the claimant's evidence is that he was dancing, enjoying the celebration when the police arrived. His evidence that police were arresting people at random clearly does not indicate that Turkish authorities had any personalized interest or were looking for him in particular. At minimum, I find that the claimant's oral testimony established that he was not "protesting" at the Newroz celebration as stated in information provided by him to immigration officials on XXXX XXXX, 2011.

propositions.text: No corroborative evidence like police report or father's signed statement supports detention claim.
propositions.quote: Notwithstanding, even if I were to accept that the claimant was in Turkey at that time and detained by police, which I do not, the claimant has not provided any corroborative evidence such as a police report or statement which he testified his father signed at his release to support this.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant was not individually targeted or tortured, was not protesting, and lacks corroborative evidence for detention claim.

propositions.text: No independent corroboration of torture; claimant did not seek medical attention, used traditional medicine.
propositions.quote: Consequently, whether the claimant was beaten and tortured has not been established by any independent corroborative evidence such as a medical report given he did not seek medical attention from a doctor nor did he attend a hospital because he was scared.

propositions.text: Unlikely police would release claimant after two days if they had interest in him or family politically.
propositions.quote: Even if I were to accept that this incident and detention occurred, which I do not, I am unable to find credible that police would release the claimant after two days if they had any particular interest in him due to his political activities or more so due to any of his family members political activities or having been addressed by police as "traitors and separatists," as stated in his narrative.

propositions.text: Counsel addressed claimant's lack of evidence supporting detention incident.
propositions.quote: Indeed, counsel addressed the claimant's lack of evidence to support this incident.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no corroboration of torture; claimant did not seek medical help; police unlikely to release him if interested; counsel noted lack of evidence.

propositions.text: Counsel questioned claimant about lack of proof of detentions; claimant said only had letter from brother, no official police documents.
propositions.quote: Counsel asked the claimant the following: Q You testified that you have no proof of your detentions. Think again. Is there anything in personal documents to show you were detained? Not official documents but... A I have a letter from my brother in Canada. Q Why do you have no official document from the police? A The Turkish police don't' give you proof even when my father signed a paper. We were afraid to ask for it.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel questioned claimant about no proof of detention; claimant said only had brother's letter, no official police documents.

propositions.text: Claimant had no criminal charges, no prosecutor or court attendance; no corroboration of detention or presence in Turkey in 2011.
propositions.quote: Notwithstanding counsel's subsequent questions and the claimant's responses that he had neither had any criminal charges laid against him nor was attended by a public prosecutor or taken to a Court, this does not provide any corroborative evidence to support his allegation that he personally had been detained by police or indeed was in Turkey in XXXX 2011.

propositions.text: Claimant provided corroborative evidence about detention of person named 'XXXX XXXX,' likely his brother, but birth dates differ.
propositions.quote: The claimant, however, was able to provide corroborative evidence14 regarding the detention of person named 'XXXX XXXX,' which counsel indicates on the index page of the claimant's personal evidence II at item 515 is the claimant's brother XXXX XXXX. While I note that the claimant does have an older brother by this name as indicated in his PIF,16 the claimant had initially listed a different birth date than that as stated in the Court decision provided.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant had no charges or court attendance; no corroboration of detention or presence in 2011; claimant provided evidence about brother's detention but birth dates differ.

propositions.text: State Security Court decision from 2003 shows public prosecution against several suspects including 'XXXX XXXX' for aiding illegal organization PKK.
propositions.quote: This decision from the State Security Court of XXXX, dated XXXX 2003, indicates that public prosecution was launched against several suspects including XXXX XXXX, on allegations that they distributed leaflets in order to facilitate the actions of illegal organizations. It states that according to article 168/2 of the Turkish Penal Code, these individuals were charged with being indirect members of the illegal organization of PKK.

propositions.text: After trial and legal amendments, suspects including 'XXXX XXXX' were acquitted of aiding illegal organization charges.
propositions.quote: The decision concludes with stating that, "after considering the trial, the defense of the suspects and the whole contents of the file, that an amendment was made under the second subsection of law 4963 and article 169 of the Turkish Penal Code, phrase 'facilitating the actions of an illegal organization' was removed from the article which resulted in acquittal of the suspects: "Therefore in the circumstances, after the amendment was made to article 169 of the Turkish Penal Code, suspects with those activities did not commit the crime of Aiding and abetting and therefore all suspects ONE BY ONE WERE ACQUITTED."

paragraphs.summary: A 2003 State Security Court decision shows prosecution and acquittal of suspects including 'XXXX XXXX' for aiding PKK.

propositions.text: Birth date and place differences exist between claimant's brother's PIF and court decision; claimant later amended birth date; no negative inference drawn.
propositions.quote: As stated earlier, the birth date of the XXXX XXXX as indicated in the above decision is that of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX1981, born in XXXX however the birth date for the claimant's brother, XXXX XXXX as stated in his PIF is XXXX XXXX XXXX/1982 and his birth place in XXXX. The claimant subsequently provided an amendment to this information in XXXX 2013 indicating that his brother XXXX was born on XXXX XXXX XXXX/1981. The claimant was not questioned regarding the difference in birth dates and places of birth (XXXX as opposed to XXXX) and consequently, I have not drawn negative inference against the claimant's credibility on this point.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes birth date and place differences for claimant's brother but draws no negative credibility inference.

propositions.text: Court decision shows 'XXXX XXXX' had lawyer, trial, and charges; claimant had no charges, so unlikely he was of police interest.
propositions.quote: The relevance of this document; however, is that the decision clearly demonstrates that a 'XXXX XXXXwas provided a lawyer and that he along with others went to court and a trial was held due to his having been charged. On balance, in the absence of any charges being laid against this particular claimant before me, I do not find it credible that he was of any particular interest to police or that if he had indeed been suspected of supporting an illegal organization, as he has alleged.

propositions.text: More likely charges would have been laid against claimant if suspected, as with 'XXXX XXXX' and others.
propositions.quote: Rather I find it is more likely than not, that charges would have been laid against him similar to that of this XXXX XXXX, and others as stated in the country condition documentation indicate.17

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant had no charges unlike 'XXXX XXXX'; likely charges would have been laid if suspected of supporting illegal organization.

propositions.text: Counsel questioned claimant about no official police documents; claimant said police don't give proof even if father signed paper; afraid to ask.
propositions.quote: Counsel again questioned the claimant regarding his not having any official document from the police to show that he had been detained. The claimant responded, "The Turkish police don't give you proof even though my father signed a paper. Also we were afraid to ask for it."

propositions.text: Claimant never charged, interviewed by prosecutor, or taken to court; Turkish system provides due process for suspects.
propositions.quote: Although counsel's subsequent questions indicated that the claimant never had criminal charges laid against him, nor was he interviewed by a public prosecutor, nor taken to court, the above decision, provides evidence to demonstrate there was due process in Turkey available for those suspected of collaborating with an illegal organization ensuring operational adequacies in place to protect the rights of those who had been arrested, charged and/or detained.

propositions.text: If 'XXXX XXXX' is claimant's brother, he remains in Turkey despite past suspicions of terrorist activity.
propositions.quote: If the above named XXXX XXXX is the claimant's brother, and if he was indeed the subject as named in the above decision, the claimant's evidence none-the-less indicates that this same brother remains in Turkey today, notwithstanding difficulties in having been suspect of terrorist activity in the past.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel questioned claimant about no police documents; claimant said police don't give proof; court finds claimant never charged; due process exists; brother remains in Turkey despite past suspicions.

propositions.text: Turkish security detains Kurds including BDP members; PKK considered terrorist; crackdown began in 2009.
propositions.quote: I accept that Turkish security forces, including police do detain Kurds, including BDP members, of which the claimant alleges to have supported, with links to the separatist Kurdish rebels.18 However notwithstanding mixed evidence regarding the treatment of Turkey's Kurdish population, the evidence clearly shows that the PKK is considered as a 'terrorist organization' by the government, and that a wider crackdown against the outlawed Kurdish rebels and their supporters began in 2009.

propositions.text: Mass trial of 205 suspects linked to KCK began July 2012; some suspects freed after months in custody.
propositions.quote: Notwithstanding mixed country condition documentation20 including that provided by counsel, I find that there is legal and judicial address for those arrested, charged and detained on accusations of ties with outlawed Kurdish rebels including, most recently as at July 2012: "On July 2, 2012, a mass trial opened in Turkey of 205 suspects - many of whom remain at large - are on trial accused of links with the Union of Kurdistan Communities (KCK), which the authorities say is the urban wing of the outlawed Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), part of a wider crackdown against what Ankara considers "terrorists" and their supporters. On July 13, 2012, an Istanbul court freed 16 suspects who are accused of ties with outlawed Kurdish rebels and had been in preventative custody for months, the state-run Antolia agency said. Among the 16 was Prof. Busra Ersani, a prominent political scientist at Marmara University, against whom the prosecution has requested a sentence of 15 years for belonging to a "terrorist organization."

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Turkish security detains Kurds including BDP members; PKK is terrorist; crackdown began 2009; mass trial in 2012 with some suspects freed.

propositions.text: Claimant did not face problems with security officials when departing Turkey eight days after alleged detention and torture in 2011.
propositions.quote: Although the claimant alleges that this last detention precipitated his flight from Turkey, he did not experience any problems with security officials when he departed Turkey, eight days after he was allegedly detained and tortured in XXXX 2011.

propositions.text: Given country evidence, claimant's ability to exit Turkey without difficulty is inconsistent with being of interest to authorities and impugns credibility.
propositions.quote: Given evidence provided in country condition documentation, particularly those pointed out by counsel in submissions,21 I do not find it credible that the claimant would have been able to pass through security checkpoints at the airport, using his own identity documents as testified if he was indeed of interest to any state authority.

propositions.text: Claimant testified airport officials checked computer files when he passed security after identity document review.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that the airport officials checked the computer files when he passed through them after reviewing his identity documents.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant faced no security problems leaving Turkey after alleged detention; this contradicts claim he was of interest to authorities.

propositions.text: Claimant's responses about identity documents at airport were evasive and inconsistent.
propositions.quote: Further, the claimant was questioned at length regarding which identity documents he provided to security at the airport when he departed in XXXX 2011. I found the claimant's responses evasive.

propositions.text: Claimant initially did not answer about airport departure but said he was detained and tortured.
propositions.quote: Initially, when asked to detail his departure at the airport in XXXX 2011, the claimant did not respond to the question posed but replied, "On XXXX XXXX XXXX 2011, I was detained and beaten and tortured, including falaka."

propositions.text: Claimant first said he did not present documents, then said he was asked for passport, ticket, and ID card.
propositions.quote: When asked if he had to present any documentation to security officials, at first he replied, No." When questioned as to whether he had to present a passport, the claimant replied, "I was asked for my passport, ticket and National Identity Card."

propositions.text: Claimant said he presented National Identity card and passed security without problems after questioning.
propositions.quote: When asked what identification he actually presented, the claimant replied that he provided his National Identity card, reiterating that he had no problems and was allowed to pass through security, after questioning.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's responses about airport identity documents were evasive; claimant gave inconsistent answers about documents presented.

propositions.text: Country evidence requires valid passport and visa to leave Turkey; claimant's claim he did not present passport is not credible.
propositions.quote: Given country condition documentation regarding22 which states specifically that "departing flight passengers must have a valid passport to leave Turkey and a visa for the country to which he or she plans to travel which must be in the passport", I am on balance, unable to find it credible that the claimant did not present a passport when he departed in XXXX 2011.

propositions.text: Claimant said airport agent arranged everything, so he had no trouble presenting passport.
propositions.quote: When questioned by counsel, the claimant maintained that he had no trouble at the airport because "the agent arranged everything."

propositions.text: Evidence indicates passenger must present own passport and ticket, contradicting claimant's claim.
propositions.quote: However, this is inconsistent with evidence which indicates that the individual must present "his or her own passport and ticket."

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's claim he did not present passport is not credible; evidence requires passengers to present own passport and ticket.

propositions.text: Claimant departed Turkey using a passport in his own name but did not list serial number or issue date in PIF question 14
propositions.quote: The claimant's evidence as indicated in his PIF at question 14 is that he departed Turkey using a passport in his own name however he does not list the serial number of the passport used or indicate when this passport was issued.

propositions.text: Claimant said he applied for and was issued passport prior to 2011 incident but no evidence of improper acquisition
propositions.quote: When questioned regarding when this passport was issued, the claimant indicated that he had applied for and was issued this passport prior to the XXXX XXXX XXXX 2011 incident however there was no evidence to indicate how it was that he had obtained it improperly.

propositions.text: Claimant testified about 2011 detention and torture but clarified departure was later that year from Istanbul with ID and passport shown without problems
propositions.quote: Q Tell me about your final departure from Turkey. A On XXXX XXXX, 2011 I was detained. I got beaten and tortured including falaka. Q I asked about your departure from Turkey not the XXXX 2011 incident. A I left Turkey on XXXX XXXX, 2011; I was in Ismit and left from Istanbul which is one hour away. Q Did you have to provide any documents to security at the airport? A No. Q You did not have to present a passport? A I was asked for my passport, identification and airline ticket. Q What identification did you present? A Turkish National Identity card Q Did you experience any problems? A No, I showed them and was able to pass through.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant used a passport but gave no serial number; claimant said passport issued before 2011 incident; claimant testified about 2011 detention and departure with ID and passport without problems.

propositions.text: Country evidence shows passport applications must be in person with police checks for criminal records or wanted status
propositions.quote: Firstly, country condition evidence23 indicates that a person must apply in person and not through an agent at the passport office of the police headquarters in the city or are in which he/she lives and that checks are made to verify whether the person has any criminal convictions and/or is wanted by authorities.

propositions.text: Claimant would not have been issued a passport in 2011 if police were interested in him for any reason
propositions.quote: Clearly, the claimant would not have been issued a passport in 2011, if the police were indeed interested in him for any reason, including any prior detentions.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds country evidence requires in-person passport application with police checks and claimant would not get passport if police wanted him.

propositions.text: If claimant used allegedly improperly obtained passport, name would be checked against centralized system at departure
propositions.quote: If the claimant did in fact use this passport which he states allegedly "improperly obtained",24 the fact remains that his name would still have been checked against a centralized computer system when he allegedly departed Turkey in XXXX 2011 to see if he was wanted for anything.

propositions.text: Claimant's allegation of being wanted is inconsistent with not being stopped or taken into custody at airport
propositions.quote: In addition to finding on balance that the claimant's allegations that he is wanted by state authorities is inconsistent with his not being stopped or taken into custody by security at the airport, the claimant indicated that he returned this passport to the smuggler who assisted him.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant's name would be checked at departure and his claim of being wanted is inconsistent with not being stopped at airport.

propositions.text: Absence of alleged new passport returned to smuggler does not reliably show claimant acquired it
propositions.quote: The absence of this alleged new passport issued sometime in 2011 which the claimant alleges to have returned to the smuggler does not provide sufficient or reliable evidence to show that the claimant actually acquired a new passport.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds absence of alleged new passport does not reliably prove claimant acquired it.

propositions.text: Only passport before panel is certified copy issued in 2010, provided after claimant expressed refugee claim
propositions.quote: The only passport before the panel is a certified copy of the claimant's passport issued in his own name on XXXX XXXX, 2010 which he provided to CIC after he had made his intention known that he wished to claim refugee protection.

propositions.text: Passport issued two days after claimant finished high school
propositions.quote: I note that the issuance date was two days after he finished high school.

propositions.text: Accept claimant was in Turkey in 2010 but no credible evidence he was there after that
propositions.quote: I accept that the claimant was in Turkey in XXXX 2010; however, I have not been provided with reliable or credible evidence to demonstrate the claimant was in Turkey after that time.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds only 2010 passport before panel, issued two days after high school, and no credible evidence claimant was in Turkey after 2010.

propositions.text: Only one stamp in passport is a visa refusal stamp from Ankara in 2010
propositions.quote: Of concern is that there is only one stamp appearing in this passport: a visa stamped XXXX Ankara XXXX appearing on page 59.

propositions.text: Claimant said visa refusal stamp made him apply for new passport after failed exit attempts
propositions.quote: The claimant indicated that it was the presence of this stamp in his passport which made him apply for the new passport sometime after his failed attempt to leave Turkey in either the Fall of 2010, as indicated in his initial PIF or on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2011, as amended later.

propositions.text: Claimant's explanation for needing new passport due to visa refusal stamp is not satisfactory
propositions.quote: I am unable to find that this provides sufficient or satisfactory explanation of reasons the claimant would need to apply for a new passport.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds only one visa refusal stamp in passport and claimant's explanation for new passport is unsatisfactory.

propositions.text: Claimant testified about trip to Venezuela via Italy, denied entry, did not exit airport
propositions.quote: Q Tell me about your trip to Venezuela. A One agent, me and five others went to Venezuela through Italy to come to Canada. We were not allowed into Venezuela. We did not exit from the airport in Venezuela.

propositions.text: Claimant said he left Turkey in 2011 using 2010 passport with police stamp
propositions.quote: Q How did you leave Turkey? A XXXX XXXX, 2011. Q What passport did you present? A The first one. Q The passport issued in XXXX 2010? A Yes. Q Was it stamped? A Yes. Q Who stamped it? A The police officer.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports claimant's testimony about Venezuela trip and leaving Turkey in 2011 with 2010 passport stamped by police.

propositions.text: Claimant likely used 2010 passport to depart for Venezuela in 2010 or 2011
propositions.quote: Given the claimant's testimony and issuance of this passport two days after completing high school, I find on balance that this would have been the passport that the claimant would have used to depart for Venezuela in the Fall of 201026 or in XXXX 2011, as per his amended PIF received in XXXX 2013.

propositions.text: No departure or re-entry stamps corroborate claimant's allegations about Venezuela trip and denied entry
propositions.quote: However, there are no departure nor re-entry stamps to corroborate the claimant's allegations regarding his attempt to flee to Venezuela in the Fall of 2010 or XXXX 2011 and his being denied entry to that country nor his re-entry to Turkey.

propositions.text: Country documents say exits from Turkey not always stamped but claimant said police stamped passport on exit
propositions.quote: Although country documentation indicates that exits from Turkey are not always indicated by way of passport stamps, the claimant when specifically questioned as to whether his passport was stamped when he exited for Venezuela testified that the police stamped his passport.

propositions.text: Absence of exit stamp undermines claimant's credibility given only stamp is visa refusal
propositions.quote: The absence of any stamp in this XXXX 2010 issued passport by Turkish authorities undermines his credibility given that the only stamp present is the above-noted visa stamp.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant likely used 2010 passport to depart Venezuela but no exit or re-entry stamps exist, undermining credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant provided a document listed as airline ticket from Turkey to Venezuela in 2011 but it is a purchase receipt
propositions.quote: Further, the claimant has provided a copy which is listed in the index of "Claimant's Personal Evidence III"27 at item two, as an "airplane ticket - Turkey to Venezuela, dated XXXX XXXX XXXX 2011." However, I note that this is not an airline ticket but the purchase of an airline ticket which does not demonstrate that it was used by the claimant.

propositions.text: Ticket does not explain claimant's inconsistent statements about travel dates to Venezuela in 2009 or 2010
propositions.quote: Further, this ticket does not provide reasons for the claimant's having stated in his initial PIF that he had left for Venezuela in the Fall of 2010 or his having indicated to immigration officials that he visited Venezuela in either 2009 or 2010.

propositions.text: Claimant told immigration officials travel year was 2009 or 2010, not 2011 as on ticket
propositions.quote: It is noteworthy that the claimant indicated to immigration officials that his date of travel was one of two years - that is: 2009 or 2010. However neither 2009 nor 2010 reflects the year 2011, the year to which the claimant amended in his PIF nor the date of XXXX XXXX XXXX 2011 as stated on the purchased ticket.

propositions.text: No reliable evidence claimant departed Turkey in 2010 or 2011 for Venezuela except his own evidence
propositions.quote: Consequently, the panel does not have any reliable evidence to show that the claimant departed Turkey in 2010 or 2011 for Venezuela other than his evidence that he did so.

propositions.text: Claimant's explanation for inconsistent dates is not accepted given PIF was completed with counsel after arrival
propositions.quote: The claimant's explanation for the inconsistent dates was because his travel to Canada was difficult and long. I do not accept this explanation given that his PIF was completed with present counsel, over one month after he arrived to Canada.

propositions.text: Evidence indicates claimant desired to leave Turkey, explaining passport application after high school, but not motivation for acquiring passport or attempts to leave
propositions.quote: At best, I find that what the evidence does indicate is that the claimant had a desire to leave Turkey which provides reasons he applied for a passport a few days after he graduated from high school. This does not however in itself provide motivation for having acquired a passport or his attempt to leave Turkey at that time.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant's airline ticket is only purchase receipt, inconsistent travel dates, no reliable evidence of departure, and claimant's explanation rejected.

propositions.text: Reason to leave Turkey in 2010 unlikely due to detentions in 2006 or 2009 given two-year delay
propositions.quote: Having reviewed the claimant's circumstances in XXXX 2010, it is reasonable to infer that the reason for his wishing to leave was not due to his having been detained in either 2006 or 2009 given the almost two year delay in departure since his last detention.

propositions.text: Relevance of failed departure attempts due to inconsistent testimony about airport events and passport stamping
propositions.quote: The relevance of discussing the claimant's failed attempt to depart Turkey is due to the claimant's inconsistent testimony regarding what indeed occurred at the airport when he departed at that time or his alleged subsequent return.

propositions.text: Claimant said passport was stamped on exit but no exit stamp exists, so no credible evidence of departure date
propositions.quote: Although he stated that this passport was stamped upon exit, as stated above, there is no exit stamp to show that it was stamped thus there is no credible or reliable evidence show when the claimant left Turkey.

propositions.text: Claimant's credibility is impugned by inconsistencies
propositions.quote: In addition, it is difficult to believe that which the claimant states because his credibility is impugned by inconsistencies.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant's reason to leave Turkey in 2010 unlikely due to delay, inconsistent testimony about passport stamping, and credibility issues.

propositions.text: Claimant said he applied for new passport because Canadian Embassy stamped first passport making it unusable for visas
propositions.quote: The claimant indicated that he had applied for a new passport, because the Canadian Embassy stamped his first passport and therefore he was unable to use it to apply for any visas.

propositions.text: Claimant's father knew an agent who helped brothers leave Turkey and advised claimant he could go with others abroad
propositions.quote: The claimant stated in his narrative that his father knew an agent given his experience in helping the claimant's brothers leave Turkey. He was advised by the agent that he could take the claimant when he was taking others abroad.

propositions.text: Claimant's chronology shows he applied for new passport before March 2011 Newroz celebration without mention of smuggler
propositions.quote: I find it interesting that the claimant indicated that his decision to leave Turkey was made at some point after (my emphasis) his failed attempt to enter Venezuela in the Fall of 2010 or XXXX 2011 but previous (my emphasis) to the March 2011 Newroz celebration, when he was allegedly picked up by police. Clearly, given the chronology as outlined in paragraph 12 of his narrative, the claimant had already applied for a new passport previous to the Newroz celebrations. There is no mention of using a smuggler or agent.

propositions.text: Claimant maintained passport was improperly obtained by agent despite country evidence requiring in-person application
propositions.quote: However, the claimant has indicated in his PIF and reiterated in testimony that this passport had been "improperly obtained." When questioned regarding what documents he had to provide in order to get this new passport, the claimant replied that his father gave the agent for ID and photos, "that was all." I find that the claimant was attempting to maintain in testimony that the passport was obtained improperly by the agent who acquired it, even though this is inconsistent with country condition documentation which indicates that acquiring a passport needs to be done in person by the individual requesting it.

propositions.text: Claimant said he departed Turkey in 2011 using passport in his name
propositions.quote: None-the-less, the claimant maintained that he departed Turkey in XXXX 2011 using a passport issued under in his name.

propositions.text: Claimant testified agent took all identity documents including Turkish ID card
propositions.quote: When asked where this new passport was today, the claimant testified that, "the agent took it. He made us give him all identity documents, including his Turkish Identification Card" (my emphasis).

propositions.text: Panel has copy of claimant's Turkish ID card provided by CIC, inconsistent with claimant's testimony
propositions.quote: Notwithstanding the claimant's testimony that he gave his Turkish Identity card to the agent who assisted him to leave Turkey, the panel has a copy of the claimant's national Turkish Identity card provided by CIC.

propositions.text: No negative inference drawn on inconsistency but claimant's claim of leaving Turkey despite being wanted is not credible
propositions.quote: Although this inconsistency was not put to the claimant, it does demonstrate another instance of corroborative evidence before the panel which in the case of the absence of an exit stamp to show when he left Turkey the first time or in this latter instance, a copy of the claimant's National Identity card. As this was not put to the claimant I do not draw negative inference against his credibility on this point however, I am unable to find it credible, as stated earlier that the claimant would have been able to leave Turkey regardless of whatever identity document he presented, whether passport or National Identity card, if he was indeed wanted due to his political activities.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant applied for new passport before March 2011, claimed improper acquisition, agent took documents, but claimant's claim of leaving Turkey despite being wanted is not credible.

propositions.text: Claimant fears detention if returned due to escape and mandatory military service
propositions.quote: The claimant fears that he will be detained if he returns to Turkey because he "escaped the country and because he will be required to do military service which means he will be forced to commit violence.

propositions.text: Claimant completed high school in 2010 and said military service was postponed while student
propositions.quote: Given the claimant's age, his completion of high school in XXXX 2010 and having reviewed military conscription requirements in Turkey,31 the claimant was asked if as a young male, was it not mandatory that he serve in the military. He replied, "I didn't want to do it." When asked if he was required, he said, "I was but my school postponed it for me while I was a student."

propositions.text: Claimant said he was given paper exempting him from military service and took university exams
propositions.quote: The claimant was asked if he had to provide documentation at the airport to show that he was exempt from military service. He testified, "I was given a paper and also I took university entry exams."

propositions.text: Claimant said he was given exemption paper in 2010 and asked brother to get another copy
propositions.quote: The claimant was asked when it was that he was given a paper excluding him from military service. He replied that he was given it in 2010 however the panel does not have any corroborative evidence regarding this. When asked about this, the claimant testified that he asked his brother to get another copy of it for him so he could present it for his hearing.

propositions.text: Claimant said airport officials checked system for military exemption and agent arranged everything
propositions.quote: When asked if he had to provide any document to security officials at the airport upon departure to show that he was exempt from military service, the claimant replied, "It shows in the system so you don't have to prove anything." His further clarification indicated that airport officials checked the computers at the airport and that he waited for a few hours but there were no problems because the agent arranged everything.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports claimant fears detention due to military service, claims exemption paper from 2010, and airport officials checked system for exemption.

propositions.text: Military exemption document dated 2012 exempts claimant until 2014
propositions.quote: The military exemption document provided by the claimant indicates it is from the Ministry of Defense, Military Draft Office, and is dated XXXX XXXX XXXX 2012, some 17 months after the claimant allegedly departed Turkey in XXXX 2011. It states that he was exempt from military procedure until the date XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX2014.

propositions.text: Claimant said he did not want to serve and was still a student
propositions.quote: The claimant was again asked reasons for the basis of his military exemption. The claimant repeated that he did not want to serve. When asked why it was that he did not go, the claimant replied, "I was still a student."

propositions.text: No evidence claimant attended school after 2010 graduation despite his claim
propositions.quote: It was pointed out to the claimant that his PIF indicates that he was not a student after XXXX 2010. The claimant replied, "When I came I was in school so I was probably wrong." There was however no evidence that the claimant attended school after having graduated in XXXX 2010.

propositions.text: Claimant said he attended military draft office in 2011 and showed paper indicating student status
propositions.quote: The claimant first indicated that he had written university entrance exams when questioned by counsel regarding his having attended a military draft office. The claimant was asked by the panel if he attended this office in XXXX 2011 when he turned 20 years of age. He indicated that he did and that he showed them a paper which indicated that he attended school, reiterating that he was still a student.

propositions.text: No credible or reliable evidence claimant was student in 2011
propositions.quote: I find that there has not been presented any credible or reliable evidence to show that the claimant was considered a student in XXXX 2011.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds military exemption document dated 2012, claimant claims student status but no credible evidence he was student in 2011.

propositions.text: No corroborative evidence claimant was student in 2011, PIF says he stopped school in 2010
propositions.quote: In the absence of any corroborative or reliable evidence to show that the claimant was a student in 2011, I assign more weight to that as stated in his PIF which indicates that he ceased attending school in XXXX 2010.

propositions.text: Claimant's actions inconsistent with being student in 2011 given passport and alleged departures
propositions.quote: Clearly, given the claimant acquired a passport in XXXX 2010 a few days after completing high school, and his evidence which indicated that he had left Turkey for Venezuela in the Fall of 2010, or XXXX 2011, I find that the claimant's actions are inconsistent with someone attending school.

propositions.text: Claimant said he did not want to attend university due to problems in Turkey
propositions.quote: The claimant when questioned on this point simply testified that he did not want to attend university due to problems at universities in Turkey.

propositions.text: Claimant's claim of being student in 2011 adversely affects credibility
propositions.quote: When the panel pointed out to the claimant that he was not a student after he completed high school in XXXX 2010, the claimant maintained that he was still a student when he attended the military branch office in XXXX 2011. I find this adversely affects his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant was not student in 2011, his actions inconsistent with student status, and this claim harms credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant's employment history shows work from 2010 to 2011 before alleged departure
propositions.quote: Further the claimant's employment history32 shows consistent employment in the XXXX industry from XXXX XXXX, 2010 until XXXX XXXX, 2011, nine days previous to his alleged departure on XXXX XXXX, 2011.

propositions.text: Claimant had no intention to attend school after high school and was not student at departure times
propositions.quote: I find on balance that the claimant had no intention of attending school in Turkey; that he did not attend further schooling after high school and that he was therefore not a student at the time he departed Turkey both the first time in the Fall of 2010 or XXXX 2011 nor when he departed in XXXX 2011.

propositions.text: No reliable evidence claimant wrote university exams or attended military branch for deferral
propositions.quote: Given the absence of any indication in his PIF that he had written university exams which may have been reason for military deferral and the absence of any reliable evidence to show that he attended this military branch for the purposes of deferring this mandatory requirement, I am unable to assign any weight to the claimant's testimony stating he attended this office in XXXX 2011 which resulted in receiving exemption from military service.

propositions.text: Claimant's contrary allegations impugn his credibility
propositions.quote: His allegations to the contrary consequently impugn his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant worked from 2010 to 2011, was not student, no evidence of military deferral, and credibility is impugned.

propositions.text: Claimant said airport officials checked system for military exemption and agent arranged everything
propositions.quote: In responses to questions regarding military exemption, according to the claimant's story, he was not questioned about a requirement for military service by airport or security officials when departing because according to the claimant, they checked the computers or because the agent was a rich man who had arranged everything.

propositions.text: Absence of alleged new passport and student visa info suggests claimant had travel visa to enter Canada legally
propositions.quote: Whether the claimant was a student or not, in the absence of the alleged new passport, to indicate that the claimant was a student, as was indicated in his passport issued in XXXX 2010, as well an absence of information provided by CIC regarding any application for a Canadian student visa in his name to enter Canada, and the absence of any evidence to show that the claimant had problems entering Canada, I find on balance it reasonable to conclude that the claimant had acquired the requisite travel visa to enter Canada on this new passport which he indicated he had applied for previous to the Newroz celebration in March 2011 and his father's making arrangements with an agent.

propositions.text: Claimant provided DHL envelope postmarked 2012 as corroborative evidence
propositions.quote: Corroborative evidence33 provided by the claimant with attached copy of DHL envelope, postmarked XXXX XXXX, 2012.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant said airport officials checked system, no student visa info, and claimant likely had travel visa to enter Canada legally.

propositions.text: Claimant provided military deferral letter dated 2012 obtained by brother
propositions.quote: The claimant has provided a document, discussed above, regarding a deferral from military conscription,34 until XXXX XXXX, 2014, which he testified was procured by his brother who attended the military draft office to get it.

propositions.text: Unlikely brother could get military exemption letter without claimant presenting documentation
propositions.quote: I do not find it credible that the claimant's brother would be able to attend a military office to obtain confirmation that the claimant was exempt from military service unless he presented some documentation to show that he was exempt.

propositions.text: Military document shows claimant had roll call in 2010 and deferral until 2013
propositions.quote: According to the above document the claimant had received a roll call on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2010 because it states he completed high school on XXXX XXXX, 2010 which resulted in his being given a deferral date until XXXX XXXX, 2013.

propositions.text: Claimant graduated in 2010 and was not student after that
propositions.quote: The claimant however completed school on XXXX XXXX, 2010 and therefore was not a student as of that date.

propositions.text: Military document exempts claimant only until 2014
propositions.quote: While he may have written university entrance exams which may provide reason for his been identified as a student on his XXXX 2010 passport, this notice from the military indicates that he is exempt only until XXXX XXXX, 2014.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant's brother unlikely to get military exemption letter without claimant's documents; exemption only until 2014.

propositions.text: Claimant provided undated letter from BDP about family problems and claimant's detentions and police beatings
propositions.quote: In addition, the claimant has provided a letter with translation from the BDP detailing problems his family experienced, particularly a brother by the name of XXXX who was an XXXX member and another brother, XXXX who was detained during his university days. This undated letter allegedly from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in the town of XXXX indicated that the claimant was "detained 2 or 3 times due to his political activities", describing his being "subject to police beatings and pepper spray" which "caused various problems for many Kurdish youth as well as for XXXX."

propositions.text: Little weight assigned to undated, unofficial letter without letterhead
propositions.quote: I assign little weight to this letter given it is undated and has been written in hand on paper without official BNP letterhead, notwithstanding it is allegedly from the Chairman of the BNP in the town of XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant's undated BDP letter about detentions and beatings is given little weight due to lack of official letterhead.

propositions.text: Claimant provided letter from half-brother dated 2012 describing police raid and detention and questioning about claimant's PKK connections
propositions.quote: As well the claimant has provided a letter from his half-brother, XXXX, which although dated XXXX XXXX, 2012, does not provide helpful information particular to the claimant's circumstances, except to state that, "...On XXXX XXXX XXXXpolice raided our home as well and they ransacked our home. Police detained me. I remained in custody for two days and police asked me many questions about you. Police asked me if you have any connection with PKK abroad and what kind of activities you do there. You are very lucky you saved yourself. I hope you will be allowed to live there and you will not face the cruelty we face all the time..."

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker notes claimant's half-brother's 2012 letter about police raid, detention, and questioning about claimant's PKK connections.

propositions.text: Half-brother was 19 when letter was written; no info on reasons for detention or status
propositions.quote: I note that this particular sibling of the claimant, according to information provided in the claimant's PIF, would have been 19 years of age when this letter was composed. There is no indication as to reasons why this brother was detained, whether he was working, attending school, in the military or exempt from the military requirements.

propositions.text: Little weight assigned to letter as it sheds little light on claimant's situation and timing is after claimant's departure
propositions.quote: I assign little weight to this letter given that it sheds little light into reasons why this brother was asked questions about the claimant or why it would be that they would consider the claimant having possible connections with the PKK abroad. It would appear from this letter that the police knew that the claimant was abroad, which is reasonable given he was cleared through security at the airport at the time of his departure in 2011. However, I find it unreasonable that the Turkish authorities would all of a sudden have interest in the claimant's alleged connection to the PKK in XXXX 2012, one and one half years after the claimant was allegedly last detained in XXXX 2011. Further, I find it strange that this letter does not speak of the police asking about other brothers during this alleged XXXX 2012 detention, particularly those remaining in Turkey, in particular the claimant's brother who held XXXX office. I cannot attach weight to a document that was written one and one half years after the claimant's departure, given all the credibility concerns with the claimant's evidence in this area.

propositions.text: Letter appears to bolster claimant's claim and negatively affects claimant's credibility
propositions.quote: I find that this letter is an attempt to bolster the claimant's claim and draw negative inference against the claimant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds half-brother's letter is of little weight, written after claimant's departure, and appears to bolster claimant's claim, harming credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant has not established a political profile or perceived one.
propositions.quote: I do not find that the claimant has established a political profile or even a perceived one.

propositions.text: Events as relayed by claimant, including detention and torture, are not believed.
propositions.quote: I do not believe that the events occurred as relayed by the claimant, particularly the claimant's testimony regarding his having been detained and tortured ("falaka") during his last detention on XXXX XXXX, 2011

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant has not established a political profile and does not believe his detention and torture testimony.

propositions.text: Security officials at Istanbul airport did not prevent claimant's departure in 2011.
propositions.quote: security officials at the Istanbul airport did not prevent the claimant's departure on XXXX XXXX, 2011.

propositions.text: Claimant's evidence about airport security was inconsistent and evasive.
propositions.quote: the claimant's evidence on this point was inconsistent... claimant reiterated that he experienced no difficulties because "everything had been arranged by the agent."

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's evidence about airport security inconsistent and notes officials did not prevent his departure.

propositions.text: Inconsistencies and evasive answers prevent assigning weight to claimant's testimony about identity documents and questioning at Istanbul airport.
propositions.quote: I am unable on balance to assign any weight to this aspect of the claimant's testimony.

propositions.text: Claimant experienced no difficulties with Turkish authorities at departure times, weighing against allegation of Turkish interest due to political activities.
propositions.quote: claimant experienced no difficulties with Turkish authorities at either of the times he departed Turkey which weighs negatively against his allegation that Turkish authorities had or continue to have any interest in him due to his political activities.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's testimony about airport questioning unreliable and no difficulties with Turkish authorities, weighing against political interest claim.

propositions.text: Claimant's attempts and documents to show Turkish interest negatively affect his credibility.
propositions.quote: claimant's attempts to testify otherwise and presentation of documentation... negatively impugns his credibility

propositions.text: No credible evidence shows Turkish authorities had interest in claimant after passport issuance or in 2011.
propositions.quote: I am unable to find no credible or trustworthy objective evidence to show that Turkish authorities had any interest in the claimant as at his departure...

propositions.text: Claimant's delay in claiming protection is inconsistent with fearing persecution.
propositions.quote: I have considerable concerns regarding the claimant's delay in claiming protection at the first available opportunity which is inconsistent with some one fearing persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's credibility negatively affected by attempts to show Turkish interest and notes delay in claiming protection inconsistent with fear.

propositions.text: Claimant's alleged travel route from Turkey to Canada is described with dates and locations.
propositions.quote: The claimant departed from Istanbul, Turkey on XXXX XXXX, 2011 by plane... crossed the border into Windsor, Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2011 in the trunk of a truck and made his claim for protection on XXXX XXXX, 2011.

propositions.text: Amended PIF indicates different durations in Cuba and Bahamas and travel by boat to Florida.
propositions.quote: The amended PIF indicates that he stayed in Cuba for 2 weeks and 2 months in Nassau before going by boat to Florida.

paragraphs.summary: The court describes claimant's alleged travel route and differences in amended PIF about durations and travel mode.

propositions.text: If claimant departed Turkey in 2011, it is unreasonable he did not seek protection at earliest opportunity after departure.
propositions.quote: I find it unreasonable that the claimant did not seek protection at the earliest opportunity after he departed Turkey.

propositions.text: Benefit of doubt given for not seeking protection in Spain as transit country.
propositions.quote: I can give the claimant benefit of doubt with regards to not seeking protection in Spain given it appears to have been a transit country to Cuba

propositions.text: Claimant did not seek protection in Cuba, Nassau or the US despite having a brother in the US.
propositions.quote: I am unable to accept that the claimant did not seek protection in Cuba, Nassau or the United States... he does also have a brother in the United States.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's failure to seek protection after Turkey departure unreasonable except in Spain, noting he has a brother in the US.

propositions.text: Claimant's failure to seek protection in US impugns credibility.
propositions.quote: The claimant's not availing himself of protection in the United States impugns his credibility.

propositions.text: Insufficient credible evidence to show claimant arrived in US as stated.
propositions.quote: panel has not been presented with sufficient credible or trustworthy evidence to show that the claimant arrived in the United States when he stated he did.

propositions.text: Negative inferences and lack of corroborative evidence undermine belief in claimant's statements about whereabouts after 2010.
propositions.quote: does not provide the panel with any comfort in believing anything the claimant has stated... no credible or reliable evidence to show where the claimant actually was after XXXX 2010.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's credibility undermined by failure to seek US protection and lack of evidence about his whereabouts after 2010.

propositions.text: Claimant's preference for Canada due to family does not excuse failure to claim protection in US despite risk to life.
propositions.quote: that the claimant would feel more comfortable in coming to Canada... does not mean the claimant should not have or could not have taken the opportunity to advance a claim in the United States

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's family ties to Canada do not justify not claiming protection in the US despite risk.

propositions.text: Federal Court case Matos Quintana supports that lack of credibility and failure to claim in US undermines claimant's credibility.
propositions.quote: it was not unreasonable to determine that... the fact that the applicant did not claim refugee status in the United States... could undermine his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Matos Quintana case supporting that failure to claim in US undermines credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant has two brothers accepted as Convention refugees in Canada and another brother accepted in US.
propositions.quote: The claimant has two brothers who have been accepted as Convention refugees in Canada and another who made a successful asylum claim in the U.S.

propositions.text: Evidence includes IRB decision and sworn declaration for brothers' refugee status.
propositions.quote: there is an IRB notice of decision for the brother... no similar notice... but counsel has provided a sworn declaration...

propositions.text: Claimant's cousin arrived in Canada in 2010 and was accepted as Convention refugee in 2011.
propositions.quote: A cousin, XXXX, arrived to Canada in 2010 and was accepted as a Convention refugee in April 2011.

propositions.text: Claimant's travel and delay in claiming protection raise questions about subjective fear of persecution.
propositions.quote: I believe that had the claimant really suffered the persecution alleged, he would have been interested in any safe destination outside Turkey, at the earliest time. I find that the subjective fear of the claimant comes into question with his actions and testimony.

propositions.text: Convention refugee requires both subjective fear and objective well-foundedness of persecution.
propositions.quote: By definition, a Convention refugee is someone who has a well-founded fear of persecution. Fear is, by its very nature, subjective, while the well-foundedness of that fear is an objective matter. Both subjective and objective components are required to meet the definition.

propositions.text: Lack of evidence on subjective element alone can cause claim to fail.
propositions.quote: A lack of evidence going to the subjective element of the claim is in itself sufficient for the claim to fail.

propositions.text: Claimant's delay in claiming protection inconsistent with subjective fear given brothers' successful claims.
propositions.quote: I am unable to find his delay in making his intention known to claim protection earlier... is inconsistent with a subjective fear.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes claimant's family refugee status, explains refugee fear elements, and finds claimant's delay inconsistent with subjective fear.

propositions.text: Contradictory testimony can cast doubt on entire oral evidence.
propositions.quote: A claimant's contradictory testimony can cast doubt upon the totality of his oral evidence.

propositions.text: Claimant has not established political profile or credible evidence of presence in Turkey after 2010.
propositions.quote: I do not find that the claimant has established a political profile... no credible or reliable evidence to show that he was in Turkey after XXXX 2010.

propositions.text: Claimant could have corroborated presence in Turkey by evidence from brother who employed him.
propositions.quote: At minimum, the claimant could have asked his brother... Given the claimant has provided letters from either brothers, I find it unreasonable not to have some record or corroborative evidence to support he worked for this company which would have place him in Turkey after XXXX 2010.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's contradictory testimony undermines credibility and no credible evidence shows presence in Turkey after 2010.

propositions.text: Claimant is Kurdish and subject to military conscription but not a person of interest to Turkish police.
propositions.quote: I do not find the claimant is a person of interest with the Turkish police. I do however believe that he is Kurdish and that he is subject to military conscription as other Turkish citizens.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant is Kurdish and subject to conscription but not of interest to police.

propositions.text: High profile politically active Kurds, especially PKK leaders, could have severe problems with Turkish government.
propositions.quote: I accept that certain high profile, politically active Kurds, and especially leaders of the Kurdistan Worker's Party (PKK) could have severe problems with the Turkish government.

propositions.text: This claimant has not established such a profile.
propositions.quote: However, this claimant has not established this profile.

paragraphs.summary: The court accepts high profile Kurds face problems but claimant has not established such a profile.

propositions.text: No evidence Kurds are persecuted as entire group; situation has improved despite problems and discrimination.
propositions.quote: There is no evidence that the Kurds are persecuted as an entire group... the treatment of the Kurdish population has improved.

propositions.text: Kurds are largest ethnic minority in Turkey, many have resettled and integrated in western cities.
propositions.quote: The Kurdish population is estimated to 10-23%... millions of Kurds... have resettled in larger western cities... and integrated well.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no evidence of group persecution of Kurds and notes their improved situation and integration.

propositions.text: Newroz cultural celebration had about 180 generally peaceful events in 2008 across Turkey.
propositions.quote: One important cultural celebration is Newroz, and it is noted in the evidence that in 2008 approximately 180 events occurred across the country and they were generally peaceful.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Newroz celebrations in 2008 were numerous and generally peaceful.

propositions.text: Turkey improved recognition of Kurdish cultural aspirations with language publications and broadcasts since 2006 and 2008.
propositions.quote: Improvements in Turkey... included, in 2006, a change to allow Kurdish language publications and television broadcasts and in 2008, a law allowing state-owned television to broadcast in Turkish.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Turkey's improvements in Kurdish cultural recognition since 2006 and 2008.

propositions.text: Claimant had no trouble getting passport and leaving Turkey; no indicators of police interest.
propositions.quote: claimant had no trouble getting a passport issued and left the country without any issues... no indicators that the claimant is of interest to the police for any reason.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant had no trouble obtaining passport or leaving Turkey and no police interest indicators.

propositions.text: Claimant states he is conscientious objector fearing military service and persecution for refusal.
propositions.quote: claimant states that he is a conscientious objector and that he fears the military in Turkey for what would be his refusal to serve on grounds of conscience

propositions.text: No reference to conscientious objection in claimant's refugee protection claim document.
propositions.quote: there is no reference to being a conscientious objector in the "Claim For Refugee Protection In Canada" document

paragraphs.summary: The court notes claimant's conscientious objector claim but finds no reference to it in his protection claim document.

propositions.text: Claimant signed declaration understanding nature and effect of information provided during examination.
propositions.quote: claimant completed and signed the declaration... indicating that the claimant understood the nature and effect of the information provided

propositions.text: It is unreasonable claimant did not include conscientious objection in fear of return when given opportunity.
propositions.quote: I do not find it reasonable for the claimant not to have included this in his fear of returning to Turkey when presented with the opportunity.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant understood examination and unreasonably omitted conscientious objection from fear reasons.

propositions.text: Claimant fears mistreatment for military evasion; harassment and discrimination exist but do not meet persecution threshold.
propositions.quote: The claimant fears that he will be mistreated for his military evasion... this does not meet the threshold of persecution.

propositions.text: Risk must be assessed forward-looking based on current events in Turkey.
propositions.quote: The definition is forward-looking, and the risk must be assessed in accordance with events in Turkey today.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's fear of mistreatment for evasion does not meet persecution threshold and risk is assessed forward-looking.

propositions.text: Claimant alleged military service deferral due to university exams until 2014
propositions.quote: This claimant alleged he was deferred military service due to having written university acceptance exams which resulted in a deferral until 2014.

propositions.text: Claimant left in 2011 despite no indicators of university attendance
propositions.quote: However, the claimant indicates that he left in XXXX 2011 even though there were no indicators that he was attending university.

propositions.text: Claimant as Turkish citizen can defer military service until age 39
propositions.quote: As a citizen of Turkey the claimant is able to have his military service deferred until age 39.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant alleges military deferral until 2014 but left in 2011 without university attendance; court notes deferral possible until age 39.

propositions.text: No alternative to military service in Turkey; draft evaders face police search and travel restrictions
propositions.quote: Those draftees who are not ready for military service have to submit their documents showing the reasons... security authorities are authorized to begin to search for these persons.

propositions.text: Draft evaders cannot travel abroad until legalizing their situation
propositions.quote: According to the Official, draft evaders (both yoklama kaçagi and bakaya) are not allowed to travel abroad until they legalize their situation (ibid.).

propositions.text: Forum 18 reports Turkish decree limits arrest of deserters to police with court warrant
propositions.quote: Forum 18... reports that... the Turkish Ministry of Justice issued a decree on 3 July 2008 which states that deserters can only be arrested with a court warrant by the police and not by the military recruitment office

paragraphs.summary: Earlier decision-maker reports no alternative military service, draft evaders face police search and travel bans; decree limits arrests to police with warrant.

propositions.text: Turkey lacks alternative military service or process to examine conscientious objection
propositions.quote: I accept that Turkey does not have an alternative to military service for those who genuinely object in serving or a process to legitimately examine the genuineness of such a military objection by virtue of conscience.

propositions.text: Government decision on military service is an operation of law
propositions.quote: However, this is a decision made by the government officials of Turkey which is an operation of law.

propositions.text: No sufficient evidence that prosecution for military non-compliance amounts to persecution
propositions.quote: I have not been provided with sufficiency of evidence that would indicate that the prosecution of the claimant for failing to comply with a military order, if such an order exists, would amount to persecution.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Turkey lacks alternative service or objection process; prosecution for military non-compliance not shown to be persecution.

propositions.text: Federal Court in Ates held repeated prosecutions of conscientious objectors do not amount to persecution
propositions.quote: In Ates, the Court stated that even in a country where military service is compulsory and where there is no alternative to military service available, the repeated prosecutions and imprisonments of a sincere conscientious objector does not amount to persecution on a Convention ground.

propositions.text: Prosecution of volunteer soldier in country with limited alternatives also not persecution
propositions.quote: If persecution does not arise in the circumstances described in Ates, then surely the prosecution and potential imprisonment of a volunteer soldier by a country that does provide some, albeit limited, alternatives to military service would similarly not amount to persecution on a Convention ground.

paragraphs.summary: Prior court held prosecutions of conscientious objectors do not constitute persecution under Convention grounds.

propositions.text: Panel not convinced claimant suffered or will suffer persecution as alleged
propositions.quote: the panel was not sufficiently convinced that the claimant encountered problems as alleged and that he suffered and would continue to suffer persecution as a result if required to return to Turkey.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds panel not convinced claimant suffered or will suffer persecution as alleged.

propositions.text: Claimant has responsibility to prove objectively identifiable risk and has not met burden
propositions.quote: The claimant has the responsibility to prove he has an objectively identifiable risk in Turkey and keeping in mind the Convention definition. The claimant has not met his burden, in the panel's view.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds claimant failed to prove objectively identifiable risk under Convention definition.

propositions.text: No successful argument made for well-founded fear of persecution or protection need under section 97 IRPA
propositions.quote: there has not been a successful argument made to suggest a positive determination in this regard.

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes no successful argument for well-founded fear of persecution or protection need under section 97 IRPA.

propositions.text: Section 97(1) requires persuasive evidence on balance of probabilities of substantial danger of torture
propositions.quote: pursuant to subsection 97(1), there must be persuasive evidence, that is on a balance of probabilities, establishing the facts on which a claimant relies, to say that he or she faces a substantial danger of being tortured on his or her return.

propositions.text: Danger must be more likely than not to be tortured or subjected to cruel treatment
propositions.quote: the danger or risk must be such that it is more likely than not that he or she would be tortured or subjected to other cruel or other degrading treatments.

propositions.text: This claim does not meet the danger or risk threshold for torture or cruel treatment
propositions.quote: This is not the case in this claim.

paragraphs.summary: Prior court law requires persuasive evidence of substantial danger of torture; court finds claim does not meet this threshold.

propositions.text: Section 97 claims must consider all relevant factors and country's human rights record
propositions.quote: a claim under section 97 must be evaluated with respect to all the relevant considerations and with a view to the country's human rights record.

propositions.text: Considering Turkey's human rights record, claimant not persuaded to face substantial danger of torture or cruel treatment
propositions.quote: I have not been persuaded that the claimant would face a substantial danger of being tortured, or that the risk and/or danger is such that it would be more likely than not that the claimant would be tortured or subjected to cruel or other degrading treatments

paragraphs.summary: Court finds claimant not at substantial danger of torture considering Turkey's human rights record and section 97 requirements.

propositions.text: Claimant is not a Convention refugee; no reasonable chance of persecution or risk of cruel treatment on return
propositions.quote: I find that the claimant is not a Convention refugee as he has not established that there is a reasonable chance or serious possibility that he would be persecuted for a Convention ground or there would be a risk to his life or he would be subjected to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment should he be required to return to Turkey in a forward looking analysis.

propositions.text: No danger of torture on return on substantial grounds
propositions.quote: On substantial grounds, there is no danger of torture should the claimant return to Turkey.

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes claimant is not a Convention refugee and no danger of torture on return to Turkey.

paragraphs.summary: Court rejects claim under sections 96 and 97(1) of IRPA.
